prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1472; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle was backing out of a space when it contacted the claimant's vehicle. Claimant reports being struck while seated in the driver's seat and has since been diagnosed with a concussion. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Initial contact made by phone; recorded statement offered and accepted.

Entry 2: Reviewed photos submitted by both parties. Visible damage to rear quarter panel of insured vehicle and front bumper of claimant vehicle is consistent with a low-speed impact. Parking lot security footage requested from the property manager. Liability appears probable but not yet confirmed pending video review.

Entry 3: Claimant provided medical records from the treating physician confirming a concussion diagnosis and recommended rest period. Claimant states symptoms include headaches and sensitivity to light. Explained the claims process and the claimant's right to seek legal advice on their own. Claimant said they understood and wished to continue handling the claim directly.

Entry 4: Parking lot security footage received and reviewed. Footage shows insured vehicle reversing without apparent check of surroundings and contacting the claimant's vehicle. Liability assessment updated to favor claimant. Requested itemized medical bills and wage loss documentation from claimant to evaluate the injury component of the claim.

Entry 5: Claimant returned the requested documentation, including medical billing statements and an employer letter confirming time missed from work. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect the concussion injury and associated treatment. Supervisor review scheduled. Claimant informed that a settlement evaluation will follow once the medical treatment status is confirmed.
